crosshair.assessment: Remote stock and native hid the reticle for the tested zero settings, view lock and held scores. At 800 × 600 the additive Vortex ring matched stock bounds at full and 62.5% charge. Native followed an accepted raw pose with interpolation disabled. Withholding both poses cleared the projection and restored body opacity. Both recovered when the raw pose returned. The ten-transition native replay used a stationary player, an instrumented pose outage and renderer state for opacity. Ordinary Forward+ geometry has visual evidence. Other weapon reticles and vehicles are separate.

scoreboard.assessment: Fully tied players retained the pinned descending client-slot order across a native reconnect. Ignore and unignore changed chat delivery and the local icon. In paired games a living player dismissed the clickable radar with Tab. For a dead player, the assigned score key temporarily hid radar and released it on key-up. Team-score tiebreaks, spectator and downloader ordering, and permanent identity-based ignores remain open. The paired checks used local multiplayer.

shownames.assessment: Paired trials exercised overlap fading, world occlusion and enemy fade-in. Native listen and remote clients hid tags behind a solid inline brush and restored them on removal. Both hid the Running Guns body and name. The stock ShowNames_Draw hook has no shipped subscriber. The native fixture ran at 20 Hz. Remote traces use mounted brushes at the last accepted pose. Under contention the listen trace can use static collision. The dark captures do not resolve the weapon silhouette.

radar.assessment: Both games recorded 36 pings on one waypoint, overlapped three pulses, wrapped the 32 slots, matched custom map bounds and brightened grey over the HUD backdrop. Paired clicks landed within 0.04 units. Native rejected a delayed visible update after the reliable clear. The joined native client also cleared six Onslaught radar links after a dropped datagram and rejected a stale graph. Frame-by-frame zoom timing and a superseded pulse during packet loss remain unmeasured.

hud.assessment: Native HUD panels are C# controls. Empty QC panel units and include fan-out do not establish coverage of the included panels.

client-routing.assessment: Client compiler aggregation is a QC build mechanism. Native client and the optional legacy CSQC VM have different entry points.

extensions.assessment: Native engine-service interfaces and the legacy CSQC extension surface are separate from QC startup extension probing and its findbox fallbacks. Compare fallback consumers rather than transplanting engine diagnostics.

constants.assessment: The pinned Gak corpse shrank from max Z 45 to 5 at the end of the death tick. Native hit traces exercised the same standing and crouched rules. Native resolves species for players and cloned bodies, reserves one abstain slot in a 20-entry ballot and resolves door targets before moving and linking start-open doors. The original uses frag sentinels for participation and the native host has explicit player state. Remote species-specific gib playback, inherited render flags and the other map initialization phases remain open.

debug.assessment: The graphical listen host labels aimed entities. Its Waypoint tool labels graph nodes. The stock producers also broadcast labels to peers. Native dedicated broadcast and legacy VM handles remain separate.

casing.assessment: Paired trials on Stormkeep verified the stock server modes, shooter and follower preferences, and in-view versus out-of-view delivery to an independent player. A native follow release between firing and sending preserved the first-person flag. The client applied the configured gun offset only outside chase view. The native pool trims on spawn and caps allocation at 1,024. Separate fixed-step tests cover ticrate and residual motion. Stock and native impact recordings resolved the shell and brass sample families. Native reads the lifetime at spawn, fades in place through the final second and gates catch-up sounds by draw time. Exact shell-tag placement, moving-brush contacts and spatial gain remain open. Native translucent batches use Godot sorting.

gibs.assessment: In seven paired lethal-hit cases, the ordinary corpse splash produced 12 models by default and 52 with EKG. Both games also tossed three separate impact chunks in those two cases. Native recorded two hit-particle requests of 200 by default and 1,000 with EKG, consistent with the executed stock branch. Both engines exercised the three gentle modes, particle-only replacement and suppression. The paired shots used human players. With normal client defaults, aligned native Original views showed Normal, gentle mode 2 and particle-only effects in both camera projections. Hiding the batch changed zero pixels under no-gibs. The other gentle modes have routing evidence; cross-engine pixel equivalence is unmeasured. Model trails, explosion push, gib audio, random sequences and end-of-life presentation retain differences or lack verification.

model-effects.assessment: The primary Fireball is the only live stock caller. The CTF shockwave is compiled out. On identical Stormkeep geometry, an eligible impact gave 28 stock observer draws and one native receipt per client. Timeout and owner self-damage produced no observed sphere. Native starts at age zero on receipt and fades the grid-lit model below 0.003 alpha. The cameras used quarter-speed game time with the native client scale set explicitly. Scene lighting and frame sampling differ. Stock linked-entity eligibility was checked in QC and the release binary. Native loopback delivered once to a peer accepted at 98 ms, and zero times at 100 or 125 ms. Native sends reliably; stock delivery depends on a gameplay datagram reaching a begun client during the window.

lightning.assessment: Compare the header's shared lightning arc API to the client effect dispatch and caller-specific beams. The declaration has no separate body to port.

rubble.assessment: The oldest listed stuck Electro orb detonated despite its later fuse. An unlisted orb and the other owner's orb survived. Each client received one impact in damage mode 0 and three after the cap was lowered in mode 2. In a second trial an orb rode a player, fell on carrier death and was evicted by the next launch. With the same muzzle offset, carrier yaw and tick rate, both orbs moved to Y 460 and their heights retained the 1/32-unit difference measured at launch. Both engines preserved the detonation deadline on carrier death. Stock showed two disconnect outcomes. Native consistently removes a freed attachment. Rotating brushes and blast presentation were outside this trial. Native casing and ordinary gib limits use independent pools.

net-notice.assessment: Both servers schedule per-recipient notices after one second. In both clients a three-second notice appeared on release from a 1.5-second hold with two seconds on its countdown and expired unseen during a four-second hold. Native used real ENet loading. Stock held the draw call after CSQC receipt. The first possible receipt during stock signon and long pre-snapshot gaps remain unmeasured.

viewloc.assessment: Both remote games placed the owner's cursor at (250,200) and (550,320) in an 800×600 view. Native aim calculations matched the sampled stock world hits. The follower saw the aimed avatar without a cursor. The stock crossing included a raw 69.7-degree frame before snapping to 90. Cursor feedback, fades and snapshot latency remain open.

common-assembly.assessment: The QC declaration and native configuration share a 30-second Xonotic default. The native ENet watchdog ends at handshake acceptance. DarkPlaces applies the connect deadline to an opened endpoint and chooses subsequent deadlines by connection state. The separate legacy client and server sample those settings on connection and on fresh traffic. The ordered report links the original/native measurements and release-version distinction.

common-state.assessment: Native keeps client preferences through respawn and observation and clears them at disconnect. The verified identity reaches the connect hooks for mute and vote privileges. A fresh client receives the pinned idle grace. Existing replacement-connection and hitplot checks cover preference isolation and writer teardown. Native map rehosting creates a new connection. Same-channel level parameter transfer and external player statistics remain separate from the local lifecycle checks.

turret-config.assessment: QC dumps and checks the turret configuration through command paths. Native turret behavior and config layering do not establish equivalent dump/check command output.

turret-weapons.assessment: These macros declare synthetic turret weapons, including weapon identity used for damage. The native turret combat and death type registry are counterparts. Verify per-weapon mapping and any visible kill-message or registry effects.

turrets.assessment: Native turrets have their own spawn and combat systems. QC registration, methods and constants need comparison at each turret and config caller.

racer-weapons.assessment: QC header declares racer weapon behavior and registration. Native Racer is the gameplay comparison point; ownership, projectile properties and weapon identity need individual checks.

raptor-weapons.assessment: QC header declares distinct Raptor gun and bomb weapon properties. Native Raptor owns vehicle fire behavior. Mapping of both paths and their metadata remains to be verified.

vehicles.assessment: Native vehicle spawn, state and HUD dispatch cover the structural responsibilities. Compare each registration and view/state consumer independently.

weapon-config.assessment: Base weapon config dump/check paths and generated cvar expansion are active mechanisms. Native weapon configuration and config-layer ADR are comparison surfaces; equivalent command behavior remains open.

weapon-electro.assessment: Header combines a registered weapon descriptor with cvars, MODE-dependent attributes and declarations. The native per-weapon implementation is the counterpart, with exact defaults, metadata and dispatch edges still open.

weapons.assessment: Generated include routing and registrations lead to the native weapon registry and typed weapon classes. Compare each registration's gameplay and ordering separately.

ecs.assessment: ADR-0007 chose typed entities over a general ECS. QC components, events, and the client frame scheduler can still drive visible movement. Compare those consumers against shared native movement, prediction and interpolation, including tick and update order.

qc-bootstrap.assessment: This aggregator also defines compiler compatibility shims, macros and shared types. The native build replaces these mechanisms. Runtime behavior in included files is tracked separately.

qc-spawnfunc.assessment: Map entities enter QC through generated spawn functions. The native map classname registry serves that role. Alias and custom-field behavior must be checked where registered.

i18n.assessment: Native localization including a PO catalog provides the comparison surface. Context, fallback and interpolation still require checks at the consuming text.

logging.assessment: Native logging replaces the QC macros. Compare format and verbosity at command and diagnostic consumers.

markdown.assessment: QC formatting helpers can affect guide/console output, regardless of their library location. Compare the concrete formatting consumers against native guide rendering.

strings.assessment: The header contains concrete implementations and macros for parsing, formatting and comparisons. C# string APIs replace parts of the mechanism, while gameplay and user-visible differences remain to be checked by caller.

promises.assessment: The QC promise mechanism is distinct from the actual asynchronous caller outcomes. Native C# execution and host services are architectural context; lifetime, error and callback behavior stay open.

qc-tests.assessment: QC test execution is infrastructure with macro registration and a distinct entry path. Native test runner and test suite replace the harness.

matrix-client.assessment: The native dedicated server implements the mx console controls, HTTP room operations and cursor-based polling. A loopback homeserver and a real native client exercised both directions, room switches, retry, token clearing and map teardown.

csqc-model.assessment: The native host owns player/model appearance and snapshot interpolation. QC headers also carry client/server callback and field contracts. The legacy client runs server-supplied CSQC separately.

warpzone.assessment: The native warpzone code and trace wrapper provide concrete runtime comparison points. QC warpzone math includes serialization, transforms and helper overloads; position/orientation and recursive-trace cases need consumer-level checks.

qc-syntax.assessment: This family contains compiler shims, references and runtime helpers. Use the file's source shape, macros and consumers to distinguish them. ADRs explain the general rewrite, with any unclassified helper behavior left open.

null-bot.assessment: The null backend's actual stub bodies are inside literal #if 0. Their file is included, but those bodies cannot run in stock SVQC. Native bot population and brain selection are separate.

bot-routing.assessment: Stock HavocBot navigation and waypoint data have native counterparts. Distinguish those callers from the optional mobile-turret A-star and the separate disabled null bot stubs.

half-life-stubs.assessment: The QC file defines inert spawn handlers for recognized imported classnames. Map loading can invoke these handlers without a literal QC call. Whether native import treats each classname with the same inert result and diagnostics remains open.

compat-quake.assessment: Native import contains Q1 remap logic. QC spawn aliases and macro-generated handlers are invoked via map classnames. Audit each remap under its format flags, particularly QC q3compat variants.

radarmap.assessment: This is the server radar-map generation command contract. Native client radar rendering is a different feature. Native command registration and generation need checking.

vote-command.assessment: Native vote controller provides a baseline for the QC vote fields, macros and command entry points. Match access rules and timing by caller.

ban-command.assessment: Native bans and command dispatch provide the comparison. Check command aliases and ban policy at consumers.

mutator-loader.assessment: QC static initialization invokes mutator loading, with dynamic registration controlled at runtime. Native GameWorld and MutatorActivation are the comparison points for first-loaded and changed state.

pathlib-debug.assessment: Debug rendering compiles only with DEBUGPATHING enabled, default 0. Its optional routines should be tracked separately from normal movement.

pathlib-utilities.assessment: location_isok is referenced by the grid routines and steerlib beamsweep. beamsweep is invoked by steerlib_beamsteer, for which the scan found no calling root. Compiled cross-file references remain distinct from a stock runtime caller.

pathlib-waypoint.assessment: The alternate waypoint search compiles. No external activation of pathlib_waypointpath was found by the source scan. It reads bot waypoint state but that does not make it the normal bot search path.

pathlib-costs.assessment: The grid A* callback implementation is compiled into SVQC. Stock mobile turret path selection links checkpoints, while A* call sites require flags that are commented out in Base. The callback binding is visible in the A* implementation.
